sections.h2: Where do Gilmer County property taxes get paid?
sections.html:
The Gilmer County Tax Commissioner collects the bill. The main office is at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540, reachable at (706) 635-4762, and the doors are open weekdays, 8:30am until 5pm. Anyone processing a vehicle title is asked to arrive by 4:30pm. The office's tax website lets owners search a parcel and pay property tax online.

Per the state revenue department, the tax commissioner collects both county and county school taxes. City taxes are different: a municipal government bills its own tax through the city clerk, unless the city and county agreed to send one combined bill. Owners inside Ellijay or East Ellijay should ask both the county office and city hall what they owe.

sections.h2: What is Gilmer County like beyond its tax office?
sections.html:
Gilmer County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of north Georgia. The legislature organized it on December 3, 1832, and Ellijay was designated seat of the county in 1834. Ellijay and East Ellijay are the incorporated cities, Cherry Log is a recognized community, and part of the Chattahoochee National Forest falls inside the borders. Its neighbors are Fannin, Dawson, Pickens, Gordon and Murray counties. Wikipedia reports 431 square miles in total, most of it cropland or forest, and notes that poultry is the biggest piece of farm output. The Apple Festival fills Ellijay each October.

QuickFacts has 33,894 people living in the county as of mid-2025, 8.1 percent above the 2020 starting count. Housing units total 19,380 and owners occupy 80.7 percent of homes. The survey median for an owner's home is $314,000, above the figure for the other two Georgia counties in the same QuickFacts comparison. Seniors account for 29.3 percent of residents, the average commute runs 28.9 minutes, and builders took out 212 permits in 2025.

With nearly three in ten residents past 65 and a commute near half an hour, Gilmer is a county where buyers weigh distance and terrain. Expect questions about road access and the lot's slope in the Blue Ridge setting.

sections.h2: Which due date will my Gilmer County bill show?
sections.html:
Read the due date on the bill itself, because Georgia lets each county pick one. The state's default for ad valorem tax is December 20, and a local governing authority may move it to December 1 or November 15 or use installment billing. After the bill is postmarked, the taxpayer gets 60 days before interest accrues.

Georgia dates that apply to a Gilmer County owner
ItemRule
Property tax returnsDue in the January through March stretch, ending April 1
Homestead applicationOpen once the home is the primary residence, through the April 1 cutoff of the first year sought
Assessment appealWritten appeal mailed with a postmark inside the 45 day window
Payment windowInterest-free period of 60 days after the bill's postmark
Refund claimMust begin inside three years after payment
Mobile home permitRequested within 30 days of placement, then again every year in the first quarter, ending April 1

Source: Georgia Department of Revenue, County Property Tax Facts for Gilmer County.

sections.h2: What if I think my Gilmer County valuation is too high?
sections.html:
Start with the yearly notice of assessment and read the appeal instructions printed on it. Under state guidance the notice has to explain how to appeal, and your written appeal must reach the assessors' board and it must carry a postmark inside 45 days of the notice mailing. The state sets that as the last day, so mark the calendar when the envelope arrives.

Call the Gilmer County assessors' office with questions about comparable sales, property record errors or what happens after a board decision. Gather these items before you call:

  • Your parcel number, found on the bill or notice.
  • Photos or invoices that show damage, a failed septic system or other condition problems.
  • Recent sale prices of similar homes nearby.
  • The postmark date on the notice envelope, if you kept it.

sections.h2: What exemptions can lower a Gilmer County tax bill?
sections.html:
Georgia requires every county to offer certain homestead exemptions, and some counties add larger local ones. Some counties take the application at the tax office and others at the assessors, so confirm with Gilmer's staff where yours is filed. The state's rule is that failure to apply counts as a waiver, so a new occupant should file before the cutoff arrives.

The same state page covers freeport exemptions on commercial and industrial inventory, which exist only where voters adopted them and are filed with the assessors. An owner of farmland or forest should ask the assessors whether a preferential assessment such as conservation use applies and which form to use.

sections.h2: Which other yearly filings affect a Gilmer County owner?
sections.html:
A few chores repeat each year and can matter at sale time. They come from the state's county facts page, so confirm details with the Ellijay office.

  • An owner who returned or paid tax last year and skips the return this year is treated as having returned the same property at last year's final value.
  • A refund request for tax that was assessed or collected wrongly has a three year window, though an appealed assessment is refunded right away once the final value is set.
  • Vehicle owners renew the tag with the tax commissioner during the 30 days that end on the owner's birthday.
  • A mobile home on the January 1 list must be returned by April 1.

sections.h2: What happens if Gilmer County taxes go unpaid before a sale?
sections.html:
The state's county facts page says unpaid taxes can collect interest after the 60 day window and may also accrue penalties. The tax commissioner is the person to ask about any balance, an execution or older years owed, at (706) 635-4762.

A seller who owes tax should get a payoff number before accepting an offer. Open tax is paid at closing from the proceeds, so a low offer on a house with several years owed may leave less cash than it appears. A mobile home is returned to the tax commissioner by April 1 each year, so a seller of one should ask whether the home and the land sit under separate accounts.

sections.h2: How does closing work on a Gilmer County house that owes tax?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax shows up in the title work, so the closing agent asks the Ellijay office for the balance and settles it at the table. Deeds go on record with the superior court clerk, and long-term notes secured by real estate carry an intangible recording tax that works out to $1.50 per $500 (or part of $500) of face value, collected by the clerk in most counties and by the tax commissioner in others. Ask in Ellijay which office takes it here.

Closing costs and who pays them are set by the contract, so read that section before signing. A written cash offer lets you compare a quick sale against a listing that could sit through a mountain winter.

We buy Gilmer County houses as-is for cash. That can suit an heir who lives out of state, a seller with a deferred roof or well problem, or an owner who needs a firm closing date with no lender conditions. If the house was left through a recorded beneficiary deed, our Georgia transfer on death page covers what the heir must record first.

faqs.q: Where is the Gilmer County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: It sits at 1 Broad Street, Suite 105, Ellijay, GA 30540, and answers at (706) 635-4762 on weekdays from 8:30am to 5pm.

faqs.q: What is the state's default due date for Georgia property tax?
faqs.a: December 20 is the statewide default. A county can set it earlier, so look at the date on your own Gilmer County bill.

faqs.q: Do I have 45 days or 60 days?
faqs.a: They measure different things. Forty-five days is the appeal clock that starts when the assessment notice is mailed, and sixty days is the grace period after a tax bill is postmarked.

faqs.q: Is Gilmer County's median home value higher than nearby counties?
faqs.a: In the Census Bureau's comparison, Gilmer's 2020 to 2024 median of $314,000 is above Gordon County's $222,900 and Glynn County's $301,300.

faqs.q: Can I apply for homestead exemption after April 1?
faqs.a: The state rule runs through April 1 of the first year, and not applying counts as a waiver. Ask the Gilmer office what it will accept after that.
